title: Hey builder, how are you gonna survive this game?
excerpt: For almost every agentic workflow today, there are 10+ alternatives. Every week, a new repo hits GitHub trending...
text:
Hey builder, how are you gonna survive this game? :: For almost every agentic workflow today, there are 10+ alternatives. Every week, a new repo hits GitHub trending that either repackages an existing harness or adds a slight UI wrapper over an existing library. How do you choose the best and keep evolving?

Here are my thoughts...
While rapid experimentation is healthy, this level of tool sprawl eats away at builder trust. When everything claims to be the "all-in-one agent platform," picking an architecture feels like a gamble.. especially for newcomers.

Over time, navigating this chaos comes down to ignoring the hype and evaluating functional boundaries through this mantra:
- Harness vs. Core: Is the repo actually solving orchestration, or is it just another frontend skin over the same backend?
- Routing & Cost Control: Where are your tokens going? Abstracting inference (via routers) saves far more time and money than swapping agent frameworks weekly.
- Lock-in vs. Portability: If a tool abstracts too much logic into proprietary primitives, swapping it out later will break your build.

Experienced builders survive the noise because they evaluate tools by constraints, not #GitHub stars. But for builders entering the space, we need fewer generic wrappers and more architectural clarity... thoughts?

title: The habit of messing around and trying new things RANDOMLY will not take you anywhere at work but it’s the opposite in your personal life
excerpt: This is a core principle I follow as well as preach.. When you do this in your personal sandbox, it works wonders...
text:
"The habit of messing around and trying new things RANDOMLY will not take you anywhere at work but it’s the opposite in your personal life"

This is a core principle I follow as well as preach..Hear me out ..
When you do this in your personal sandbox, it works wonders:
• The blast radius of failure is zero.
• You have the absolute liberty to fail fast, learn, and grow.
• You can connect random dots across any domain without answering to anyone.
Curiosity needs no ROI when the only stakeholder is yourself.

Bring that exact same loose mindset into work, though, and it backfires.
Not every company encourages open-ended experimentation. The moment you start casually messing around with random tools or ideas, it's easy for leadership to make quick judgments that you are unfocused and going nowhere.

Here's the cheat sheet I follow to try new things at work without burning credibility:
1. Stay strictly domain-aligned - Anchor your experiment directly to the exact workflow, pipeline, or problem the team is already solving.
2. Bring data and proof, not just excitement - Show up with: "Here was the bottleneck. I tested approach A vs. B in our setup, and here are the numbers proving it works."
3. Define the kill switch early - Know upfront when an approach isn't working and pull the plug before it eats up team bandwidth.

title: Typing slows you down.. Dictate ALWAYS wins and makes you 10x
excerpt: I recently listened to an interview with the CEO of Conductor who mandated a fascinating Workflow for his entire team...
text:
Typing slows you down.. Dictate ALWAYS wins and makes you 10x..
I recently listened to an interview with the CEO of Conductor who mandated a fascinating #Workflow for his entire team: everyone is equipped with the exact same #Microphone setup.

Their primary input method is Dictation..
It sounds simple, but it is a fantastic way to accelerate #Productivity. You don't have to keep swapping windows, struggling with syntax, or interrupting your flow state.
You just speak your thoughts out loud, moving fluidly from one #Idea to the next while the system processes everything in the background.

But the real advantage isn't just speed; it’s intent. Modern #LLMs are incredibly adept at understanding the nuances of how we speak. When you are explaining a complex #ProductManagement concept or a new #SoftwareEngineering architecture out loud, you naturally use more expressive language. You pause. You emphasize.

That raw, unfiltered context is critical. It allows the #AI to better empathize with your intent and generate far superior options compared to a sanitized, heavily edited text prompt.

title: Never hand a deterministic task to a probabilistic model
excerpt: I was at a talk recently where I shared this strong perspective: Never hand a deterministic task to a probabilistic model..!
text:
I was at a talk recently where I shared this strong perspective: Never hand a deterministic task to a probabilistic model..! to help people realize a hard truth: many teams are trying to employ LLMs for absolutely anything and everything.

Everyone wants to use LLMs as a magical silver bullet. But if you don't know what your platform can do without an AI model, you are setting yourself up to fail.

LLMs are incredible for creative, open-ended problem-solving. However, blindly funneling every single task whether hosted locally or on a massive GPU cluster into an LLM is a scalability nightmare waiting to happen.

This is the fundamental to excel & overcome the problem I was talking about:
• Platform Mastery First: You need hands-on, deep-in-the-weeds knowledge of your platform's native capabilities before you ever touch an AI integration.
• The Deterministic Divide: Know exactly what should be written as standard, deterministic automation by your team versus what genuinely requires an LLM.
• Earn the LLM: Using an LLM should be a deliberate architectural choice, not a lazy default because a team didn't want to learn the platform's intricacies.

title: The AI hype train is officially out of fuel
excerpt: Remember a couple of months ago when everyone was obsessing over that Reddit-style platform where AI agents just talked to each other?
text:
The AI hype train is officially out of fuel.. Remember a couple of months ago when everyone was obsessing over that #Reddit-style platform where AI #agents just talked to each other?

Influencers milked it for engagement, the headlines went crazy, and people were calling it the absolute peak of interesting AI innovation.
But if you look at the real-world utility of that experiment? Literally zero.

I see this happening in companies every single day. People build flashy, one-off AI experiments, pat themselves on the back for "innovating," and completely miss the mark on ROI.

- If it doesn't solve a real problem for you or your customer, it's just noise.
- I constantly debate this with folks—not to shoot down their ideas, but to push them toward doing the right stuff. We need to stop building vanity projects and start harnessing AI practically.

Here is what actual, tangible AI innovation looks like:
Build for Modularity: Create reusable components that provoke new ideas, not isolated silos.
Solve Repetitive Pain Points: Look at the actual, exhausting bottlenecks in a workflow and build solutions specifically for them.
Demand Provable Output: If you can't point to a clear, tangible result, there is no need to continue the project.

#Innovation isn't about getting 30 seconds of fame on a timeline; it's about making a sustainable impact. Stop building for the applause. Start building for value.

title: Software decisions are never made in a vacuum
excerpt: Sometimes, a single update designed to protect users is exactly what drives them away..
text:
Software decisions are never made in a vacuum. Sometimes, a single update designed to "protect" users is exactly what drives them away..

Lately, I’ve been thinking a lot about the second-order effects of product decisions.. specifically, how platforms balance user convenience, ecosystem health, and their own revenue.

We are seeing two massive paradigm shifts happen right in front of us:
1. The Browser Ecosystem & Chrome 150: Google’s recent push to phase out Manifest V2 under the banner of security and privacy effectively neutralizes many popular ad-blocking extensions. The intended result is a more controlled extension environment and a likely significant bump in ad revenue. The second-order effect is power users will migrate to Brave, Firefox, and Opera.
2. The AI Search Paradox & The Creator Squeeze: As an end-user, getting an immediate, AI-synthesized answer without clicking a link is phenomenal. But websites invest in high-quality content relying on page views, while AI mode parses this data and serves it directly to the user. Zero clicks for the creator. The platform captures attention while the original creator gets starved of traffic.

title: Kunal Shah's Secret Chess Move at WhatsApp: Meta just dropped $900M into CRED
excerpt: Since its mid year, I have decided its time to place a virtual bet here. My Bet: Meta will entirely route WhatsApp UPI into CredUPI...
text:
Since its mid year, I have decided its time to place a virtual bet here. Kunal Shah’s Secret Chess Move at #WhatsApp: Meta just dropped $900M into CRED, and Kunal Shah is moving to Menlo Park as the global head of WhatsApp.

My Bet: Meta will entirely route or deeply embed WhatsApp UPI into CredUPI, making premium, high-reward payments the default native experience. This move isn’t just a random experiment. It is a highly calculated strike leveraging a massive regulatory shift and hyper-native consumer psychology.

1. The NPCI "Silent Golden Goose" - The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has a strict 30% market share cap timeline for third-party UPI apps. Google Pay and PhonePe (holding ~80% combined) are operating under a ceiling. Meanwhile, NPCI completely lifted user onboarding restrictions for WhatsApp Pay. Kunal is stepping into a perfect market vacuum.
2. Shifting from Mass Market to Native Dopamine Loops - By injecting CredUPI, Kunal brings CRED’s reward psychology into your chat thread. You pay a business natively inside WhatsApp, instantly unlock CRED coins and premium vouchers. Suddenly, transacting on WhatsApp isn't a utility chore—it's a high-dopamine habit loop directly in your inbox.
3. The Conversational Commerce Expansion - With WhatsApp's powerful business ad infrastructure, this unified engine will seamlessly drive users into high-intent actions, booking luxury travel, purchasing gold ETFs, or transacting with premium D2C brands, all inside a single conversational flow.

Kunal Shah is a distribution-first thinker. He knows you don't beat a utility giant by copying their scanner; you beat them by changing the incentive layer and keeping the user captive in the inbox. Let’s see how this bet ages over the coming quarters.

title: Some of the world’s greatest software is being completely rewritten right now
excerpt: Not by massive tech corporations, but by solo developers armed with an LLM and an obsession...
text:
Some of the world’s greatest software is being completely rewritten right now.
Not by massive tech corporations, but by solo developers armed with an #LLM and an #obsession.
Take the recent buzz around the #SQLite rewrite in #Rust.. SQLite is one of the most widely deployed pieces of software on Earth, but its codebase has historically been closed to outside contributors. Now, a passionate developer is building a modern, community-driven alternative.

But what catches my eye is the "Why now?" For years, developers have harbored deep-seated feelings for legacy software—wishing they could optimize it, but blocked by massive architectural complexity. Enter Generative AI as the ultimate companion. When you pair an obsessed builder who deeply understands a problem with an AI that can deconstruct monolithic logic and handle boilerplate, the traditional barriers to entry evaporate.
